title: Copilot desktop app can read open tabs in its built-in browser as page context (rolling out now)
summary: MC1552386: from mid to late November 2026 (worldwide), the Microsoft 365 Copilot desktop app uses content from open webpage tabs in its built-in browser as context for questions and summaries, on one tab or across several. Microsoft says page context is scoped to the current conversation and is only active when the built-in browser is enabled; if it is disabled, nothing changes. Microsoft's compliance notes confirm this modifies AI capabilities that interact with customer data.
why: Anything a user has open in that browser, including internal web apps, admin portals or third-party SaaS, can now become prompt context. That is a data-flow change for your AI governance record and DLP assumptions, even though Microsoft marks it 'no action required'.
todo: Confirm whether the Copilot desktop app's built-in browser is enabled in your tenant and for which users.
Record the change in your AI service register and check that your Copilot acceptable-use guidance covers browsing context.
Pilot with a small group and check what Purview audit captures for these interactions before broad exposure.
Tell helpdesk that context is per conversation, so 'Copilot remembered my tab' questions have an answer.
